text: But now they laugh at me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with the dogs of my flock.
What use to me was the strength of their hands? All their vigor had perished.
Gaunt from want and hunger, they gnawed the parched ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.
They picked saltwort among the bushes, and the roots of the broom tree were their bread.
They were driven out from among people, shouted at as if they were thieves,
forced to live in dry riverbeds, in holes in the ground and among the rocks.
Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they huddled together.
A senseless brood, sons of nobodies, they were whipped out of the land.
And now I am their taunting song; I have become a byword among them.
They loathe me and keep their distance; they do not hold back from spitting in my face.
Because God has loosed my bowstring and afflicted me, they cast off the bridle before me.

versions.text: Because God has loosed my cord and humbled me, they throw off all restraint before me.
versions.explanation: עִנָּה here means 'afflicted/brought low by suffering' rather than 'humbled' (which suggests moral humbling); and רֶסֶן is a specific image (bridle) that the vague 'all restraint' loses. 'Bowstring' also clarifies the metaphor of lost strength.

text: On my right the rabble rises up; they trip my feet and throw up their siege ramps against me.
They tear up my path; they further my ruin, and no one need help them.

versions.text: They tear up my path; they profit from my ruin, and no one holds them back.
versions.explanation: Two points: (1) יֹעִילוּ with לְהַוָּתִי means they 'further/promote' his destruction rather than 'profit from' it; (2) לֹא עֹזֵר לָמוֹ literally means 'there is no helper for them' — i.e., they need no one's help — not that no one restrains them. 'No one holds them back' reverses the sense of the clause.

versions.text: They tear up my path; they push forward my ruin, and they need no help to do it.
versions.explanation: The sense is accurate, but 'push forward my ruin' is an awkward collocation for oral reading; 'further my ruin' renders יֹעִילוּ לְהַוָּתִי idiomatically, and the shorter final clause keeps the line's rhythm while preserving the corrected sense of לֹא עֹזֵר לָמוֹ ('they have no need of a helper').

text: They come on as through a wide breach; amid the crash they roll in upon me.
Terrors are turned loose against me; my dignity is driven off like the wind, and my deliverance passes by like a cloud.
And now my life is poured out within me; days of affliction have taken hold of me.
Night pierces my bones; the pains that gnaw me never rest.
With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me tight like the collar of my tunic.
He has thrown me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to you, and you do not answer; I stand before you, and you only look at me.
You have turned cruel toward me; with the strength of your hand you assail me.
You lift me up to the wind and make me ride it; you melt me away in the roar of the storm.

versions.text: You lift me up to the wind and make me ride it; you toss me about in the roar of the storm.
versions.explanation: מוג in the Poel means 'dissolve, melt away', a stronger image of being undone than the generic 'toss me about', and it preserves the parallel progression from being carried off to being destroyed.

text: For I know you will bring me down to death, to the house appointed for all the living.
Yet surely no one lays a hand on a man in ruins, when in his disaster he cries for help.
Did I not weep for the one whose days were hard? Was not my soul grieved for the poor?
But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness fell.
My insides churn and will not be still; days of affliction confront me.
I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
My skin turns black and peels away, and my bones burn with fever.
My lyre is tuned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of weeping.
